description:
## What

PKIX-fmtv.2 (CLOSED 2026-05-12) ratified adding an `AiaFetcher` trait for online intermediate retrieval per RFC 5280 §4.2.2.1, alongside SignatureVerifier and RevocationChecker. The .2 closure deferred all downstream shape decisions (trait location, sync vs async, error type, failure-mode contract, caching contract, HTTP impl crate location) to implementation children.

AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 (added 2026-05-12) adds a hard requirement: trait + result types must be cache-friendly. This bead captures that constraint so it lands on whatever implementation epic eventually files the AiaFetcher work.

## Constraints the AiaFetcher trait MUST satisfy

- **Trait shape admits caching wrappers.** Method signature is `fn fetch(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AiaError>` (or async equivalent), with `&self` (not `&mut self`) so a caller can wrap with Arc-based caches. Don't bake in state that prevents this.

- **Error type is cache-friendly.** `AiaError` derives `Clone + Debug + PartialEq + Eq + non_exhaustive`, is `Send + Sync`, supports serde behind the workspace's serde feature flag. Don't embed std::io::Error directly (not Clone); flatten / wrap.

- **Fetcher impls can be either sync or async.** Mirror the pkix-revocation / pkix-revocation-http split: sync trait in core no_std-friendly crate; async variant in std-only adapter crate.

- **Empty default (`NoAiaFetcher`) returns an error rather than panicking.** Caller treats missing-intermediate as a failure mode, not a fetch attempt. Cache-friendliness implies this naturally — the no-op fetcher should be a zero-cost wrapper that emits a deterministic error.

- **Batch fetch SHOULD be admitted at the trait level if the implementation can do better than N sequential fetches.** Real consumer: certs with multiple AIA URIs to try in fallback order; HTTP fetcher could pipeline. Not required (callers can loop) but the trait shouldn't preclude it.

## Out of scope

This bead does not file the AiaFetcher implementation work. It captures the design constraint for whoever does. Close this bead when the AiaFetcher implementation epic/bead is filed AND its description references these constraints. Alternative: include the constraints by reference in the implementation epic's description so this bead can close immediately.

## Why human-labeled

Decision-gate: when the AiaFetcher implementation work is decomposed, sync/async/error-type/caching-contract choices need to satisfy these constraints. Reviewer of the implementation epic confirms compliance before closing this bead.

## Cross-references

- PKIX-fmtv.2 (CLOSED 2026-05-12, decided to add the trait)
- AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 (cache/batch/prevalidation rule)
- Memory pkix-caching-batch-prevalidation-2026-05-12
- pkix-revocation-http::extract_aia_http_urls (already exists, gives ca_issuers list per cert)

[2026-05-13 closed: superseded by PKIX-zkjb]

PKIX-zkjb filed 2026-05-13 as the AiaFetcher implementation epic. All five cache-friendliness constraints from this bead reproduced verbatim in PKIX-zkjb's description under 'Cache-friendliness constraints (from PKIX-8uyr, MUSTs)'. The constraint-capture mission of this bead is now fulfilled by PKIX-zkjb's existence.

PKIX-zkjb.1 filed as the one open sub-decision (trait location: pkix-aia vs pkix-chain vs pkix-revocation). Mark to decide; recommendation is (i) pkix-aia.

PKIX-zkjb children .2-.7 not yet filed — autonomous loop can decompose as it works through the epic after .1 lands.

Closing this bead as superseded. Implementation work tracked under PKIX-zkjb.
title: AiaFetcher trait design must satisfy AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 (cache-friendly)
